subject.title: Control UI: Memory panel for MEMORY.md and USER.md

question: Should OpenClaw add a narrow core Control UI Memory editor for `USER.md`, root `MEMORY.md`, and daily memory notes now, defer it to Control UI plugin contribution slots, or fold it into broader workspace file management?
rationale: The request changes browser access to prompt-influencing persistent state and overlaps active workspace CRUD and plugin UI extension designs, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent security and product boundary.

options.title: Approve Narrow Core Memory Panel
options.body: Add a small core surface that edits only reviewed memory files and date-scoped daily notes with explicit authorization, path/date validation, UI proof, and gateway safety tests.

options.title: Defer To Plugin Contribution Slots
options.body: Keep the feature behind the Control UI contribution-slot design so a memory/context plugin can provide a host-rendered panel without another one-off core UI contract.

options.title: Fold Into Workspace CRUD
options.body: Treat this as a specialized view on top of the broader workspace file-management API after that security model is approved and landed.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow Core Memory Panel
recommendation.body: Add a small core surface that edits only reviewed memory files and date-scoped daily notes with explicit authorization, path/date validation, UI proof, and gateway safety tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal is ownership of the read-only workspace RPC boundary and adjacent gateway protocol documentation this decision would extend.
